predecessors.name: Fourteenth Dynasty of Egypt
predecessors.text: Avaris and the eastern Delta, the seat of the Fourteenth Dynasty, 'which the Hyksos replaced'

predecessors.name: Middle Kingdom of Egypt
predecessors.text: Memphis, the Delta and Middle Egypt up to Cusae, where the Hyksos 'expanded to occupy Memphis'

successors.name: New Kingdom of Egypt
successors.text: Egypt reunited under Ahmose I, who took Avaris and then Sharuhen near Gaza

ledger.x: c. 1650 BC: the Hyksos set up the Fifteenth Dynasty at Avaris. Infobox 'fl. c. 1650 - c. 1550 BC', capital Avaris, 'Preceded by Fourteenth Dynasty (based at Avaris, which the Hyksos replaced)'; Fifteenth Dynasty page 'Established 1650 BC'. The page names Avaris, not a boundary.

c. 1650 BC: the Hyksos take Memphis and Lower Egypt from the Thirteenth Dynasty. Fifteenth Dynasty page: the dynasty 'expanded to occupy Memphis', which led to the fall of the Thirteenth Dynasty there (no year given). The Hyksos page says direct control was 'probably limited to the eastern Nile delta' and the infobox…

c. 1650 BC (undated): Sharuhen is a Hyksos stronghold. Ahmose I page: he 'completed his victory over the Hyksos by conquering their stronghold Sharuhen near Gaza after a three-year siege'; the Hyksos page says 'some scholars argue' it 'was a city in Canaan under Hyksos control'. No year for its acquisition; set at the…

c. 1630 BC: the Hyksos reach Thebes and clash with its king. Fifteenth Dynasty page: the dynasty, 'after a period of about 20 years since its foundation, extended its rule as far south as Thebes', 'entering into conflict with Pharaoh Neferhotep III'. The year is 1650 less 20; the pages do not say which dynasty…

c. 1629 BC: no lasting Hyksos hold on Thebes. PAGE CONFLICT: the Fifteenth Dynasty page says the dynasty 'extended its rule as far south as Thebes'; the Hyksos page puts 'their southern border' 'at Hermopolis and Cusae' and Ryholt calls Theban vassalage 'a baseless assumption'. This dossier follows the Hyksos page: no…

c. 1553 BC: Kamose of Thebes opens the war of reconquest in the Cusae-Hermopolis borderland. 'In Kamose's third year, he embarked on his military campaign against the Hyksos'; reign 'c. 1555 - 1550 BC' puts year 3 at c. 1553. The Hyksos page instead dates the Kamose campaign 'c. 1542 BC' and the Second Intermediate…
c. 1550 BC: the war ends in the Theban reconquest of Egypt under Ahmose I. Kamose page: 'his full brother made the final conquest of them and united all of Egypt'; Kamose 'Died: 1550 BC'.

c. 1550 BC: Ahmose I conquers Avaris and ends Hyksos rule in Egypt. 'After this, in the fourth attack, he conquered the city'; Hyksos rule ended by Ahmose's year 18 or 19 at the latest, and Sharuhen near Gaza fell last 'after a three-year siege' (undated). The year is the Hyksos infobox's c. 1550 BC; the Hyksos page…

c. 1550 BC: the Hyksos kingdom ends. Infobox 'fl. c. 1650 - c. 1550 BC', 'Succeeded by Eighteenth Dynasty, founded by Ahmose I'; 'Manetho says the Hyksos were allowed to leave after a treaty' while Bietak argues 'many Asiatics were resettled elsewhere in Egypt'.

wars.name: Theban-Hyksos war
wars.outcome: Seqenenre Tao 'started a series of wars against the Hyksos and perished in battle'; Kamose 'continued the war'; Ahmose I conquered Avaris in his fourth attack and then Sharuhen, and reunited Egypt.

wars.name: Siege of Sharuhen
wars.outcome: Ahmose I 'completed his victory over the Hyksos by conquering their stronghold Sharuhen near Gaza after a three-year siege.'
